title: Python SDK: stream iterator + event-router ergonomics and retry surface
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Deliver a polished, ergonomic streaming chat surface in the Python SDK that unifies event dispatching (token/partial/structured events), provides a simple async iterator + context manager, and exposes a clear retry/resume surface for transient network or model-side interruptions. This ticket focuses on the API shape, compatibility with existing sync and async codepaths, and example snippets for docs and migration notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Provide an async iterator API that yields Event objects and a small set of helpers (messages(), text(), structured()) for common consumption patterns.
- Offer a context-manager that closes the websocket/stream on exit and flushes metrics.
- Design a retry/resume policy surface: max_attempts, resume_token_hint, on_retry callback, and idempotency guidance for partial responses.
- Expose backpressure signals to allow callers to await when processing is slow (basic flow control).
- Include 3 examples in docs: naive consumption, structured output handler, resumable consumer with local checkpointing.

Design notes:
- Keep default behavior conservative: single automatic retry for transient network errors; do not auto-retry on user-provided function/tool calls or when structured output has already been emitted.
- Use an explicit EventRouter object rather than implicit callbacks so applications can plug-in middleware (logging, metrics, transform).
- Maintain a small sync wrapper that calls the async API for users on legacy code.

API proposal (first draft):
```
from redwood import StreamingChat

async with StreamingChat.stream(model="redwood-2.1", retry_policy={"max_attempts": 2}) as stream:
    # stream.events() yields a sequence of Event objects: Token, Delta, ToolCall, Structured
    async for ev in stream.events():
        if ev.type == "token":
            print(ev.text, end="", flush=True)
        elif ev.type == "structured":
            process_structured(ev.json)

# convenience helper for message-level iteration
async with StreamingChat.stream(model="r2") as stream:
    async for message in stream.messages():
        handle_message(message)
```

Resumable/retry surface example:
```
# resumed consumer holds a local checkpoint: last_seq_id
async with StreamingChat.stream(model="r2", resume_from=last_seq_id) as s:
    try:
        async for ev in s.events():
            last_seq_id = ev.seq_id
            process(ev)
    except StreamInterrupted as e:
        # on interruption we can resume using last_seq_id
        schedule_resume(last_seq_id)
```

Migration notes: callers currently using lower-level on_event callbacks should map to EventRouter by creating a lightweight router adapter. Keep handler compatibility for a transitional period (one release).

Telemetry: emit metrics for streaming_sessions.total, streaming_sessions.retries, streaming_sessions.resume_success, and event_processing.latency.

Open questions:
- Should retry_policy allow model-variant fallback (e.g., to a cheaper model) or is that handled solely by server-side routing? (Prefer server-side, but allow an opt-in parameter later.)
- How aggressive should default flow-control be? For now, provide an awaitable stream.pause() API and document common patterns.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ava Martinez: Spike complete. Implemented PoC async iterator and basic Event class (Token/Delta/Tool/Structured). Observed that TLS re-negotiation in our test harness causes a mid-stream disconnect that must be surfaced as StreamInterrupted.

2026-02-20 - Ravi Patel: Reviewed PoC. Suggest splitting EventRouter from transport to make unit testing easier. Also: add on_retry callback to allow apps to surface UX messaging (e.g., 'Reconnecting...').
2026-02-24 - Design (Maya Chen): UX thumbs up for context-manager API. Asked for one-line convenience helpers for common cases (text-only stream and messages()).
2026-03-01 - Eng infra (Leo Nguyen): Confirmed telemetry tags we can expose. Added a note to ensure retries increment cost metrics for user billing visibility.

2026-03-05 - Ravi Patel: Implemented initial API in branch github.com/redwood/inference/tree/feature/ENG-19876-stream-ux. Open PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4987. Unit tests for iterator/backpressure are green locally but flaky in CI (timeout on slow runners).

2026-03-09 - QA (Sofia Alvarez): Found race where stream.pause()/resume() ordering can deadlock if called after transport closed. Recommending a guard that no-ops after terminal state. Added test case in tests/streaming/test_pause_resume.py
2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel: Addressed QA race and added docs examples. Preparing for design review on 2026-03-15. Next: sync wrapper and migration guide, then canary docs rollout.
